MUNICH, Germany, Oct 20 : Bayern Munich could be without coach Vincent Kompany, first-choice goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and playmaker Joshua Kimmich when they host Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, assistant coach Aaron Danks said on Tuesday. Kompany is nursing a virus that has affected his legs at times, while Neuer has only just recovered from a minor injury and Kimmich missed training due to personal reasons, Danks told a press conference. "Vince has had a virus, and it is important for him to rest," Danks said. "So he is at home. We are taking it day by day. He will play his role in the game whether in the Allianz Arena or not." As for Neuer, no decision has yet been made, Danks said, with the keeper back in training for the past two days. Kimmich's participation is equally unclear.

"For Joshua it is personal reasons. I am not sure what it means for tomorrow," Danks added. Bayern, already without suspended Michael Olise, want to bounce back in the competition after last week's 3-3 draw against Viking in Norway, and have been boosted by a 6-1 demolition of RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday. "The key will be decided on small margins," Danks said. "We have to be prepared for every aspect of the game. "We trust the process and the work we have done with the players in the last couple of seasons. We want them to play fearless and express themselves."

Oct 20 : Aston Villa right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka will be out for three to four weeks with a hamstring injury, while midfielder Johan Manzambi has also been sidelined with a minor knock, manager Unai Emery said on Tuesday. Both players were injured in Saturday's 1-0 Premier League win at Newcastle United, where Manzambi scored the winner in the first half. “Manzambi has a small injury, he’s not available for tomorrow," Emery told a press conference ahead of Villa hosting Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday. “Aaron has an injury as well, more or less we expect three or four weeks."

Oct 20 : Turkey have appointed Sergen Yalcin as head coach on a four-year contract to replace the sacked Italian Vincenzo Montella, the country's football federation (TFF) announced on Tuesday. The 53-year-old former Turkey midfielder steps into the job following Montella's dismissal earlier this month after a difficult UEFA Nations League campaign. Turkey sit bottom of Group A1 after four consecutive losses, having also suffered a group stage exit from the 2026 World Cup. "We wish Yalcin success in his new role and hope this decision proves auspicious for our country and our national team," the TFF said in a statement.

Oct 20 : It was a difficult, almost incomprehensible, feat. A band of seafarers from Easter Island in the South Pacific set off in double-hulled sailing canoes on a voyage across Earth's largest ocean that ended more than 4,400 miles (7,100 km) away in Hawaii, the only Polynesian island in the Northern Hemisphere. But this oceanic odyssey centuries ago was no myth. New genetic research has determined that Native Hawaiians are genetically most closely related to the people of Easter Island, also called Rapa Nui. "Using whole genomes, our algorithms can find DNA sequences matching perfectly between individuals on different islands, the legacy of common ancestors. From these data we can create family trees of the islands," said Stanford University computational geneticist Alexander Ioannidis, co-senior author of the study published in the journal Science.  The findings point to a founding population of people from Easter Island arriving in Hawaii as the first humans to settle the lush volcanic island chain.

The data indicated that the people who settled Easter Island arrived there in the 1200s after journeying from Mangareva island in French Polynesia, more than 1,500 miles (2,400 km) away, and that a subset of them subsequently set off for Hawaii. That voyage likely occurred in the same century, Ioannidis said. "We examined shared segments of DNA, genetic variation and thousands of reconstructed family trees. In 61 per cent of those trees, Hawaii and Rapa Nui were paired together. We checked it four different ways because, frankly, we were dumbfounded and couldn't believe it ourselves at first," said genome scientist and study co-senior author Keolu Fox of the University of California, San Diego. It would have been an incredible journey, Ioannidis said. "In their canoes, they brought with them plants that they would need on the newly settled island, and they included bananas, taro and sweet potato, as well as animals like the chicken. It is believed that the Polynesians would embark on these voyages across thousands of miles of ocean in order to discover new islands rich in resources and land to settle," Ioannidis said. The researchers pieced together these long-ago journeys based on genetic data revealing the relatedness of present-day people from various Polynesian islands, analyzing DNA from more than 1,000 Polynesian people. These included 317 Native Hawaiians, 12 Rapa Nui and 8 Mangarevans, as well as others from the Society, Tuamotu, Marquesas, Austral, Samoan and Tongan islands. The genetic data showed Mangarevan ancestry was second only to Easter Island ancestry for Native Hawaiians. MONUMENTAL SEA CROSSINGS The researchers attribute these monumental sea crossings to an ultravoyaging population they call Holomoana Nui, the Hawaiian phrase for "great ocean voyaging," with Hawaii as the last destination reached. They were the greatest voyaging community in human history, according to Fox, who is a Native Hawaiian. "Polynesians were exploring and settling the Pacific centuries before Europeans began their celebrated voyages of discovery," Fox said. "Perhaps it's time to rethink who we call explorers." Using genetic data, the researchers previously tracked how Polynesian voyagers reached a succession of islands over a period of centuries in one of the most impressive settlement feats in human history, but that study traced them only as far as Easter Island. THE FOUNDING OF TAHITI The new study included a detailed genomic analysis of people from Tahiti, one of the Society Islands and the locale for which the researchers had the most genomes. They were able to estimate the size and date of the founding generation — roughly 800 people reaching Tahiti around the year 1070. "Since the voyage to Hawaii was much longer, we would expect its founding population size to have been no larger and likely smaller," Ioannidis said. Native Hawaiians and Easter Islanders share many cultural traits found among eastern Polynesians, including a similar Austronesian language and similar foods, Ioannidis said. The study has implications for disease risk among Native Hawaiians and other Polynesians due to genetic bottlenecks called "founder effects." These arise when a small portion of a population separates and founds a new population, as the Polynesians did each time they ventured to and settled on a new island. This narrowing of the gene pool can amplify the frequency of some rare genetic variants sometimes related to diseases, while others vanish entirely, Ioannidis said. The Polynesians repeated the pattern of settling on new lands, intensifying the effect. "Repeated founder effects concentrated rare disease-associated variants in Polynesian populations. We identified variants linked to kidney disease and blindness that occur at surprisingly high frequencies in French Polynesia," Fox said. Founder effects have been extensively studied in certain populations including the Amish, Ashkenazi Jews and Finns, leading to standard screenings for certain genetic conditions for them. "Why not Hawaiians?" Fox asked.

Source: Reuters

Oct 20 : Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has blamed Cristiano Ronaldo's lack of fitness and preparation for the forward's struggles during his second stint at the club, saying the Portugal international "let the team down." Ronaldo won three Premier League titles under Alex Ferguson before leaving United for Real Madrid in 2009, and returned to Old Trafford in 2021. But under Dutchman Ten Hag, Ronaldo struggled in the 2022-23 season, scoring once in 10 league appearances before leaving the club in November 2022. "He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag told The Athletic in an interview published on Tuesday.

Reuters has contacted Ronaldo's representatives for comment. Ten Hag, who guided United to a third-place league finish in 2022-23, said he had confronted Ronaldo about the player's performance. "Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score.' He was not capable to do this," said Ten Hag, who was sacked by United in 2024. "It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself." Ronaldo joined Saudi club Al-Nassr in December 2022 and scored 14 league goals in 16 appearances before the end of the season. "Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in," said Ten Hag. Ronaldo, Portugal's all-time leading scorer with 146 goals, was handed a 30-day ban by the country's football federation on Monday after he left the national team camp following a rift with coach Jorge Jesus. The 41-year-old forward is expected to play for Al-Nassr in a Saudi Pro League game later on Tuesday. He is 19 goals short of scoring 1,000 in his career.

Source: Reuters

Oct 20 : Salesforce said on Tuesday it would acquire Braze in a deal valued at about $5.66 billion, eyeing the New York-based company's AI-driven personalization tools to strengthen its business software offerings. The deal is the latest bet by Salesforce to accelerate its AI transition as investors worry that the rapid adoption of the technology could erode demand for traditional software. Braze Class A shareholders will receive $47.50 in cash per share held, representing a premium of about 58.1 per cent to the stock's last close. Shares of Braze jumped more than 50 per cent in early trading while Salesforce's stock dipped.

Braze's AI tools help marketers optimize content, offers, channels and timing, and let brands send personalized messages to customers and respond to their behavior in real time. The company serves about 2,770 customers including Canva, Dairy Queen, Equinox, Instacart, Urban Outfitters and Venmo. The transaction is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal year 2028, subject to required approvals. The company does not expect the deal to change its fiscal 2027 forecast. Salesforce has been doubling down on its AI offering and signed a $3.6 billion deal for AI agent platform Fin earlier this year and an $8 billion deal for Informatica last year. Salesforce would pay a $300 million termination fee, while Braze would pay $191.4 million if it abandons the deal. J.P. Morgan Securities is the exclusive financial adviser to Salesforce, while Qatalyst Partners is advising Braze.

NEW YORK, Oct 20 : The US dollar slipped on Tuesday as doubts over the AI trade resurfaced, while the euro edged up despite traders' lingering worries about unrest in France. Shares in South Korean AI services firm Elice Group plunged 32 per cent in their Seoul market debut, a sign that negative sentiment toward the AI sector in global markets is not easing. Strong capital inflows into US stocks have supported the dollar. Higher interest rates, driven partly by growth and inflation expectations tied to the sector, have also helped. "The dollar has been supported by big inflows into the equity market," said Dominic Bunning, head of G10 FX strategy at Nomura.

Now, he said, "there is a lot more skepticism about the degree to which a lot of these companies will be profitable enough to justify the amount of issuance that having to be made at the moment … and whether this whole ecosystem can be profitable enough in the context of higher rates over a period of time." The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.27 per cent to 101.69, with the euro up 0.2 per cent at $1.1232. Traders remained wary of the euro despite Tuesday's modest gains as France faces widespread protests and a worsening fiscal picture. The government said overnight curfews in violence-hit areas of France's biggest cities had brought some respite from the country's worst unrest in years. More protests are planned for the weekend. "The worries in France are not going away anytime soon," said Tommy von Brömsen, FX strategist at Handelsbanken. "The bearish view on France will stay for a while longer, and there's much more euro weakness to be priced in." Britain's pound strengthened 0.66 per cent to $1.339 after labour market data showed a resilient jobs market, the latest batch of data from the UK that surprised to the upside. "The risk is that a resilient labour market gives the Bank of England both the room and the reason to raise interest rates again," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro. "Sterling could benefit from rising rate expectations." Markets are almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Bank of England at its next meeting on November 5, according to LSEG data. STRONG JAPANESE BOND AUCTION The yen jumped after an auction of longer-dated Japanese government bonds (JGBs) drew record demand.  "The record 20-year auction is a strong signal that sidelined cash is finally coming back," said Masahiko Loo, senior fixed-income strategist at State Street Investment Management in Tokyo. "JGBs are also starting to look like a relative haven from Europe's political and fiscal volatility, particularly around France.” The Japanese yen gained 0.29 per cent against the greenback to 158.04 per dollar.  Elsewhere, the Canadian dollar rose 0.42 per cent to 1.405 per US dollar, its strongest level in almost a month, after Alberta residents voted by a large majority to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation.

Oct 20 : Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November. The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said. The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could not immediately determine the scale of the cuts. Qualcomm did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September.

One of the world's biggest smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets. Its shares have risen just 1.5 per cent in 2026, compared with gains of more than 12 per cent for the benchmark S&P 500 and nearly 60 per cent for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index. Qualcomm shares were up more than 1 per cent after trading down about 0.5 per cent earlier on Tuesday. In its latest earnings report in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-center and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. The company expects the majority of its chip sales to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as it expands into the fast-growing AI data-center market. Amon said in the memo business priorities, organizational needs, skills and expertise would be considered in making the cuts. "As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require," he wrote. "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed."
